questions.question: What does this MR add and why?
questions.answer: It adds reliable webhook delivery: shipment events are enqueued into a new webhook_deliveries table for each active endpoint, and a polling worker POSTs signed payloads with retries and exponential backoff, moving a delivery to a dead state after max attempts.

questions.question: What is the riskiest or most questionable part a reviewer should scrutinize?
questions.answer: claimDue marks rows in_flight when it claims them, but there is no lease, timeout or reaper: if a worker crashes or a status write fails after claiming, the delivery stays in_flight forever and is never retried, since the worker and the index only look at pending rows.

questions.question: What happens when an endpoint returns a 500, and when does a delivery go dead?
questions.answer: On a failure the delivery returns to pending with attempts incremented and next_attempt_at set by exponential backoff (5s base, doubling, capped at 6 hours). Once attempts reach maxAttempts (8 by default) it is marked dead instead; every non-2xx or network error is retried, including 4xx.

questions.question: Where do the retry delay computation and the claim query live?
questions.answer: retryDelayMs and nextAttemptAt are in src/webhooks/backoff.ts; claimDue (UPDATE ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) and the mark functions are in src/webhooks/repository.ts; the loop is in src/webhooks/worker.ts.

questions.question: What design question should a reviewer raise about the retry design?
questions.answer: Backoff has no jitter and all failures, including permanent 4xx like 410, are retried for the full schedule; the dead letter is only a status on the same table with manual replay, and enqueue happens outside any transaction with the event insert (event can be saved without deliveries). The stuck in_flight problem is the main one.
must_mention: enqueue not transactional with event insert
